answer: Price each new identity by the square of how many its funder already made: the first costs a coin, the tenth a hundred, the hundredth ten thousand. Funders are traced through their payments, so a sybil farmer spinning up a thousand fakes faces a bill that climbs like a dune, not a line. One honest agent pays once, a velvet-soft fee, and works in the oasis of cheap trust, while each fake needs an opal-priced ticket; the quadratic wall makes the farm cost more than any reward it could harvest.
